heroHeadline: Ukraine Drones Strike Russian Military Training Ground in Retaliation for Kyiv Blitz Ahead of NATO Summit
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,564 (June 7, 2026), the Ukraine war diplomacy collapsed within 48 hours of its most dramatic overture of the year. President Zelensky's June 4 open letter to Putin — proposing a direct bilateral meeting, immediate ceasefire, and all-for-all POW exchange — was rejected by Putin on June 5-6, who called the letter 'rude' and said he saw 'no point' in meeting before a comprehensive deal was pre-agreed. On June 6, Putin simultaneously held a private Kremlin meeting with former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder (potential backchannel mediator), which the EU's Kallas immediately rejected as compromised. As diplomacy stalled, Ukraine launched its second major drone strike on St. Petersburg and Kronstadt naval base in one week (the first timed to SPIEF's opening on June 3; the second as it closed), with Russia claiming 376 drones were intercepted overnight — potentially the largest single Ukrainian drone operation of the war. Russia retaliated by launching 272 drones against Ukraine (249 downed by the Air Force), killing 3 and wounding 4+ across Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions. On the frontline, ISW confirmed Russian advances in Pokrovsk and Slovyansk while Ukraine held Kostiantynivka. Russia pressed in Sumy and Kharkiv oblasts seeking a ~20 km buffer zone. The US House advanced the Ukraine Support Act ($8B military financing), Germany announced its largest-ever single Ukraine aid package (€11.5B), and NATO targeted $15B additional for 2026. Russian cumulative losses reached ~1,373,620 by June 7.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, Euronews, PBS NewsHour, GlobalSecurity.org, United24 Media, Wikipedia War Timeline, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
